newsitem.title: UK: Dixon Motor posts good August after H1 jump.
newsitem.headline: Dixon Motor posts good August after H1 jump.

text.p: Motor retailer Dixon Motors Plc said its sales were strong in August, which traditionally sees a big spike in UK retail car sales because of the change in the British registration plate letter.
Chief executive Paul Dixon told Reuters in an interview that combined sales on new and used cars were up around 25 percent compared with August 1995.
But Dixon described the August rush to buy as "hard work" and said he supports moves to change the system.
"(A change) will benefit the industry as a whole, Dixon said. "It would also create greater opportunities for selling used cars."
Earlier, Dixon posted an 85 percent jump in pre-tax profits in the first half to 2.35 million stg from 1.27 million last year and raised its dividend by 19.4 percent to 2.0p per share.
Dixon said the figures showed the companies commitment to its commercial strategy was working.
"We are now reaping the dividends of strategic investments over the last two to three years," Dixon said. "We're also well positioned to take advantage as the economy improves."
Dixon said the integration of Gordon Plunkett was going well adding that the GPG management have already put forward ideas for expansion.
He added that Dixon itself is also looking for further acquisitions.
"Lots of opportunities are crossing my desk but they will have to meet our criteria," Dixon said.
Dixon predicted that the current 7,000 UK retail motor outlets would be reduced to around 4,000 by the year 2000.
